title: Matching Shingles After a Repair
description: A new bundle will not match shingles that have weathered in the Houston sun. The patch should be planned before it is visible from the street.
html:
The repair can be watertight and still look wrong. New asphalt is darker, the granules sit higher, and the color name on the wrapper is a factory mix, not a promise to match a roof that has spent eight summers facing west. Anyone who tells you the patch will disappear is selling the repair twice.

Why the same color is not the same color

Shingles fade. The sun cooks the asphalt, dust fills the granule, and algae darkens the shade slopes. A bundle made this month, even in the same brand and color, sits next to that and reads as a rectangle. Different plants, and discontinued colors, make it worse. Some of the laminates on Houston houses from the last fifteen years are simply gone. There is no secret supplier with a perfect match. There is salvage, blend, or an honest patch.

For a small repair on the street face, we pull usable shingles from a rear slope or a spot above the eaves you do not see, and we put the new bundle where the eye does not land. That only works when the old shingles are still flexible enough to lift. Brittle shingles break when you un-nail them, and then the repair grows. We will tell you that before we start, not after the slope is a checkerboard.

When a patch is the wrong shape

A few courses around a boot can be a repair you live with. A third of the front slope in a different dye lot is a repair you will hate every time you pull in. At that size, replacing the slope, or the roof, looks cleaner and ages on one clock. Repair or replace is the decision. Matching is just the part you can see from the curb.

Ask, before the ladder goes up, where the shingles are coming from and what the street will look like. If you want that answer from us, roof repair starts with a look, not a bundle on the truck. Call (281) 541-0027 or request a free inspection.
